paragraphs.text: Profile-level skill manager for DeepSeek Harness: a flat skill inventory with enable/disable, discov
ery diagnostics and a restorable trash, in a sidebar panel.
# dsh-skill-mgr
**Every skill in one list** — the whole profile inventory in a sidebar panel: see what is installed,
read a skill's body, enable or disable it, repair a discovery problem, and delete it into a trash y
ou can restore from.
**English** | 简体中文
> If this plugin saves you a hunt through `~/.dsh/skills`, a ⭐ star helps the next person find it.
## Why this exists
A skill is a folder with a discovery file in it, which is easy to create and hard to keep track of:
which ones exist, which are currently switched off (a renamed file is invisible, not absent), which
one has a broken frontmatter, and which are duplicates across the two writable roots. This plugin is
the one place that answers those questions, without an editor open and without hand-renaming files.
**Enabled is the default, and disabling is a filesystem fact first.** The discovery file is renamed
(`SKILL.md` → `SKILL.md.disabled`, or `<name>.md` → `<name>.md.disabled`) so the filesystem provider
simply stops seeing it; a registry record is what lets the panel still list it and switch it back o
imply stops seeing it; a registry record is what lets the panel still list it and switch it back on.
## Screenshots
*Skills — one flat table over the profile inventory (enabled and disabled alike), with search, a sou
rce filter, use-count and last-used chips, the discovery diagnostics and the restorable trash.*
*Inspect — the skill's body and metadata, with the enable/disable action for a disabled skill.*
## The registry file
[代码示例省略，未执行]
One registry holds everything the manager persists: the disabled-skill records, the trash, and the s
tatistics checkpoint. It is reconciled at startup — a `.disabled` file with no record is adopted (an
upgraded or hand-edited install), and a record whose file is gone is dropped. Writes go through an
atomic same-directory temp file (`wx`, mode `0600`, then `rename`), and a read that hits unparsable
JSON refuses to overwrite it and reports why.
## Features
| Surface | What it does |
| Sidebar row | sits directly under **Plugins** (`order: 1`) and opens the **Skills** page in the ce

ntre column |
| Skills table | one flat table of the profile inventory — Name / Source / Description

/ Status / Actions — with search, sorting and a source filter |
| Enable / disable | renames the di

scovery file and keeps the record, so the row stays visible (dimmed) and can be switched back on |
|

Inspect | reads a skill's body and metadata without leaving the GUI |
| Add skill | scaffolds a new

skill in a writable root |
| Discovery diagnostics | lists the skills the provider cannot see, and

auto-fixes the repairable ones in place |
| Restorable trash | `Delete` moves a skill into the root'

s `.trash`; the panel lists it with a Restore action, and clearing the trash is explicit |
| Chat `/
` menu dots | marks each candidate row as model-invocable or user-invocable, coloured from the same

settings the panel reads |
| Settings card | the plugin's own configuration, in the Plugins manager

|
| Attribution | the title chip carries the installed version and the author credit |
## Requirements

- Node.js `>=24.9.0`
- A DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` installation (the plugin composes into a prof

ile)
- `pnpm` 11.20.0 (`packageManager` in the manifest pins it)
## Installation
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DeepSeek Harness afterwards; the sidebar entry appears directly under **Plugins**.
The package is not on npm: the profile installs it from this repository. `dsh plugin` (a pnpm passth
rough into the profile directory) is what the script uses, and the Plugins page does the same thing.
The desktop profile is owned by the Electron application, so `dsh --profile desktop` itself refuses
to compose it, while `dsh plugin` still works.
Upgrading from `dsh-skill-hub`? The two packages must not both be installed — they would both claim
the plugin-config card. Remove the old bundle first; the new plugin adopts the old state file on its
first load and leaves it untouched.
## Quick start
1. Open **Skills** in the sidebar. The table lists every skill in `~/.dsh/skills` and `~/.agents/ski

lls`.
2. Search for a skill; select **Inspect** to read it, or **Disable** to switch it off for the

whole profile.
3. Select **Add skill** to scaffold a new one in a writable root.
4. Read the diagnos
tics banner when something is not being discovered, and use its fix action on the repairable entries
ics banner when something is not being discovered, and use its fix action on the repairable entries.
## Configuration
The Loader entry's config is the settings card; the host reads the same values through their volatil
der entry's config is the settings card; the host reads the same values through their volatile refs.
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `enabled` | `true` | contribute the skill provider and the announcement; the management panel keep

s working either way, because it is the surface that turns the plugin back on |
[该节后续省略]
## Caveats
- **Enable/disable is profile-wide, not per workspace.** Because toggling renames one discovery file
, there is no way to have a skill on in one workspace and off in another; every workspace is offered
every skill in the profile inventory. A reader who needs per-workspace on/off cannot have it here.
- **Project skills are discovered, not managed.** The provider lists a workspace's own roots so an a
gent still sees the skills beside it, but they are never part of the profile inventory the panel man
ages: they cannot be toggled, deleted or adopted. Only `~/.dsh/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` are wr

itable.
- **Writable roots are user-level only**, and a refusal names the source that owns the skill

.
- **Deletion is recoverable but has no automatic expiry.** `Delete` moves the skill into the root'
s `.trash` directory and the panel lists it with a Restore action; clearing the trash is permanent.
- **A local install pins the tarball's path.** Delete `dist/dsh-skill-mgr-<version>.tgz` and the nex

t install fails with `ENOENT`.
- **There is no update check.** This package is heavily refactored fr
om `dsh-skill-hub`, so tracking upstream releases would be misleading and there is no release channe
l of this package to poll.
